thread.title: Technology Sector Update for 07/26/2018: QCOM, NXPI, FB

title: Technology Sector Update for 07/26/2018: QCOM, NXPI, FB
text:
Shutterstock photo Top Tech Stocks
MSFT -0.75%
AAPL -0.04%
IBM +0.53%
CSCO +1.03%
GOOG flat
Technology stocks were falling hard Thursday after Facebook disappointed Wall Street with its Q2 revenue and daily active users growth. At last look, shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 were losing almost 1.4% in value although the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was posting a nearly 1.5% gain.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ Qualcomm ( QCOM ) rose 5% after the specialty chipmaker late Wedneday said it was scrapping its proposed $43 billion acquisition of rival semiconductor firm NXP Semiconductor ( NXPI ) and will instead buy back up to $30 billion of its common shares. It also reported Q3 results easily beating Wall Street forecasts, including net income of $1.01 per share during the three months ended June 24 and topping the Capital IQ consensus by $0.30 per share. Non-GAAP revenue totaled $5.63 billion, also exceeding the $5.19 billion analyst mean.
- Separately, NXP Semiconductor ( NXPI ) retreated to a 22-month low on Thursday, sinking over 8% to its worst share price since September 2016 at $90.25 a share after the chipmaker missed Wall Street forecasts with its Q2 financial results by wide margins in addition to Qualcomm cancelling its planned merger. It earned $0.16 per share on $2.29 billion in sales during the three months ended June 30, missing the Capital IQ consensus expecting a $0.37 per share Q2 profit on $2.36 billion in revenue. The company received a $2 billion break-up fee from Qualcomm overnight and the NXP board authorized a new, $5 billion stock buyback.
In other sector news:
- Facebook ( FB ) dropped nearly 20% on Thursday, losing almost $130 billion of its former value and weighing on the broader averages after the social networking company late Wednesday reported Q2 revenue and daily active users missing analyst expectations. Revenue grew 42% year-over-year to $13.2 billion, lagging the $13.3 billion Street view. Daily active users also rose 11% over year-ago levels, averaging 1.47 billion in June, but slowed from 17% growth during the same quarter last year. It also earned $1.74 per share, topping the Capital IQ consensus of $1.70 per share.
